clamp.description: A firm squeeze built up slowly and released just as slowly.
clamp.howTo: Tighten slowly over 3 seconds as the circle fills, then release just as slowly as it empties. Keep the movement smooth in both directions.
clamp.name: Clamp

downstairs.description: Squeeze to the top, then come down one step at a time under full control.
downstairs.howTo: Squeeze to your strongest, then relax a little at a time, pausing about one second at each level on the way down. The controlled descent is the exercise.
downstairs.name: Downstairs

elevator.description: The signature exercise. Climb up step by step, then come back down under control.
elevator.howTo: Imagine riding an elevator. Tighten a little more at each step until you reach your strongest squeeze, then come back down one step at a time until fully relaxed.
elevator.name: Elevator
elevator.summary: Climb to the top, then step back down

flash.description: The fastest flicks. Short snappy squeezes that train quick reactions.
flash.howTo: Squeeze and let go as fast as you can, in time with the circle. Stay light, do not strain.
flash.name: Flash

front-clamp.description: A slow, focused squeeze of the front pelvic floor with a quick clean release.
front-clamp.howTo: Tighten slowly over 3 seconds as the circle fills. When it empties, let go all at once. Then start the next slow squeeze.
front-clamp.name: Front Clamp
front-clamp.summary: Squeeze up slowly, let go at once

holding.description: Squeeze and keep holding to build baseline endurance in the pelvic floor.
holding.howTo: Squeeze your pelvic floor and keep holding for the whole round. If the tension fades, gently squeeze back up. Keep breathing normally.
holding.name: Holding

long-steady-clamp.description: The endurance builder: a one second squeeze into a ten second full-strength hold.
long-steady-clamp.howTo: Tighten for one second, then hold at full strength for ten seconds. If the tension fades, gently squeeze back up to full. Let go and repeat.
long-steady-clamp.name: Long Steady Clamp

pulsation.description: Two quick squeezes back to back, then a complete release. Trains squeezing again before you have fully recovered, and letting go properly between efforts.
pulsation.howTo: Squeeze and release twice in quick succession with the circle, then let everything go completely while it rests. The full release matters as much as the pulses.
pulsation.name: Double Pulse
pulsation.summary: Two fast pulses, then a full reset

push.description: Build the squeeze to a strong peak, hold it, then let go slowly.
push.howTo: Tighten gradually over three seconds, getting stronger as the circle fills. Hold your strongest squeeze for two seconds, then release slowly. Squeeze harder, never push down or strain.
push.name: Push

reverse-clamp.description: A quick squeeze followed by a slow, controlled letting go. Great for control.
reverse-clamp.howTo: Squeeze at once, then immediately start releasing as slowly as you can, following the circle down. The slow letting go is the exercise.
reverse-clamp.name: Reverse Clamp

short-holding.description: A strong 4 second hold released slowly rather than dropped. Letting go under control is a skill in its own right, and most people find it harder than the hold.
short-holding.howTo: Tighten over one second, hold at full strength for four, then release gradually as the circle sinks. Do not let it collapse - stay with it all the way down.
short-holding.name: Short Holding

starter.description: One quick squeeze to wake the muscle, then a strong 5 second hold.
starter.howTo: Give one quick squeeze, relax smoothly, then squeeze again and hold strong for five seconds. Let go, breathe, and repeat.
starter.name: Starter
starter.summary: Quick flick, then a 5 second hold

steady-clamp.description: A steady clamp: squeeze for a second, then hold at full strength for five.
steady-clamp.howTo: Tighten for one second, then hold at full strength for five seconds without letting the tension drop. Let go and repeat.
steady-clamp.name: Steady Clamp

steady-trembling.description: Squeeze at once, keep the tension steady for a couple of seconds, then relax.
steady-trembling.howTo: Squeeze at once and hold the tension. When the circle drops, let go smoothly. Then repeat the quick squeeze and hold.
steady-trembling.name: Steady Trembling
steady-trembling.summary: Squeeze at once, hold, then relax

trembling.description: Rapid on and off squeezes that make the muscle tremble and wake up its fast response.
trembling.howTo: Squeeze all at once, hold for a moment, then let go smoothly. Follow the circle as it snaps up and eases down.
trembling.name: Trembling

upstairs.description: Climb the squeeze in four steps, a little stronger at each level.
upstairs.howTo: Imagine riding an elevator upward. Tighten a little, then more, then more, until you reach your strongest squeeze, spending about one second at each level. Relax afterward.
upstairs.name: Upstairs

waves.description: Wave-like squeezes that build and release tension continuously.
waves.howTo: Tighten slowly for two seconds, then release just as slowly, like a wave rising and falling. Keep it smooth and continuous.
waves.name: Waves

4.description: Longer sessions for stronger muscles. 4 minutes.
4.name: Level 4

find.onlyDoThePeeTest: Only do the pee test once
find.onlyDoThePeeTestDesc: It is just a way to find the muscles, not an exercise. Stopping your pee often is not good for your bladder.
find.squeezeOnlyThoseMusclesDesc: Another cue: squeeze as if holding back gas. Your belly, legs and buttocks stay completely relaxed.
find.stopTheFlowBody: Next time you pee, gently stop the flow midway. The muscles you just used are your pelvic floor.
find.thatExactSqueezeIsThe: That exact squeeze is the move you will train.
find.theEasiestWayToFind: The easiest way to find them
find.tryItNowBody: Press and hold the circle. While you hold it, squeeze those muscles. Let go together.
find.youFoundThemBody: That squeeze and release is all a Kegel is. You are ready for your first exercise.

first.followTheCircle: Follow the circle. Squeeze... and relax.
first.tenSecondsReady: Ten seconds of {{exercise}}. Squeeze on every {{contract}}, let go on {{relax}}. Ready?
first.thatWasARealExercise: That was a real exercise. Every session works exactly like this, one circle at a time.
first.theCircleIsYourGuideBody: Every exercise follows this circle. When it glows and swells, squeeze. When the glow fades, relax. The word inside always tells you what to do.
first.yourFirstExerciseQuickFlicks: Your first exercise: quick flicks. Squeeze on Contract, let go on Relax.

onboarding.slide1Body: Nobody talks about them. They trace back to one weak muscle, and a weak muscle can be trained back.
onboarding.slide2Body: No gym, no equipment, nothing to take off. On the sofa, at your desk, on the bus. Nobody can tell.
onboarding.slide3Body: The app tracks how long you can hold. Your times climb, new exercises unlock, and the change shows up where you wanted it.
onboarding.slide3Title: You feel it before you see it
onboarding.slide4Body: Stop training and the muscle fades, the same as any other. Pick a time, and let the reminder handle the rest.
onboarding.slide4Title: It only works if you keep going

why.andYouCanDoIt: And you can do it anywhere, anytime. Sitting, standing, on the bus. Nobody can tell.
why.benefit_confidence_desc: Gains that build week after week.
why.benefit_performance_desc: More control and stamina in intimacy.
why.learnItOnceAndEvery: Learn it once, and every minute you train actually counts.
why.squeezeTheWrongMusclesAnd: Squeeze the wrong muscles and you get nothing back.
